prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, showing which firms export and how reallocation across firms creates new channels for the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single part on B010, credited to Helpman and Melitz. The exchange tested it on the points that could have moved me, and it held. The first test is distinctness from the 2008 prize. Representative-firm new trade theory cannot generate selection into exporting, exporter premia, entry and exit of firms, or within-industry reallocation after liberalisation. The heterogeneous-firm framework generates all four, and they are separately testable. Firm-level data across many countries have been used to test them. That is the standard I apply to any candidate, whatever its field: a transparent mechanism, credible evidence that confronts it, and a record of replication and extension. B010 meets it, and I do not need field balance to carry the case. The second test is attribution. Melitz (2003) is the identifiable origin of the selection mechanism. Helpman's firm-level work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, extends it into firm boundaries and multinational activity, so a two-name credit follows the intellectual structure. In answer to the chair's wording question, I would keep the citation to selection, reallocation and gains from trade. I would not make it a career-wide citation for Helpman, and I would not credit Redding. The scientific background should acknowledge Bernard-Jensen on exporter facts, Eaton-Kortum on the quantitative strand, and Hopenhayn on firm dynamics. The third test is maturity. More than twenty years of extension leave no age concern. What the round-1 exchange changed is how I describe the caveats, not the choice. The qualitative selection and reallocation result is the discovery. The size of the welfare gains is a separate, model-sensitive question, and the citation should not claim a number.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still credit. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Hopenhayn are real precursors or parallel contributors, and a two-name award omits them. Wording and the scientific background can acknowledge them, but they cannot fully repair the omission. A second reservation is that the quantitative gains depend on parametric structure. Under Pareto productivity draws, some sufficient-statistic results suggest the extra gains from selection can be small relative to simpler models, and later work reports larger gains under other distributions. This is from my recollection and I have not verified it. It supports keeping the citation on the mechanism and not on welfare magnitudes. A third is field balance after the 2008 trade prize. I do not think it should decide among candidates, but I accept that other members may weigh it, and I cannot show that it carries no weight in the Committee's judgement. If the Committee finds B010 too close to earlier trade recognition, B019 is my strongest alternative. Its conceptual importance is high and its credit core is clean. The open questions there are the boundary of the credit with the accelerator strand and the adjacency to the 2022 prize.

responses.point: Boppart ranked B010 sixth in his opening but now treats it as a serious alternative. He keeps B019 as his preferred part because it has a tighter single-mechanism attribution, and he sees B010 as having real credit disputes with the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum strand.
responses.response: I accept that B019 is a single mechanism with two clear originators, and I opened with it first for that reason. We now differ mainly on how to weigh a clean mechanism against a larger confirming record. My weight falls on the confirming record, since it shows the mechanism has been confronted with data. The Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum dispute is real, but I think it is narrower than it looks. Bernard-Jensen documented the exporter facts and Eaton-Kortum built a parallel quantitative framework. Neither supplied the selection-and-reallocation model that Melitz did, and the citation can be worded to avoid claiming it did. I would not call B010's credit clean. I would call it defensible, and the omissions can be stated openly in the background document. I also agree that your move on B010 is a judgment between two strong candidates, not a disagreement about quality.

responses.point: Strömberg narrowed B019 to Kiyotaki and Moore after discussion, citing my point about the accelerator strand and 2022. He says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010, and he regards B010 as possibly the safer case.
responses.response: Your move to two names is the one I think makes B019 most defensible, and we now agree on the credit core. On order, I put B010 first because the evidence for its mechanism is more direct. Exporter selection and reallocation are observable in firm-level data, while the collateral-amplification channel has to be inferred through quantitative models and crisis episodes. You describe the 2022 mechanisms as distinct, with Kiyotaki-Moore concerning collateral values and asset prices in the real economy. I find that persuasive, and it is why B019 stays my first alternative. If the Committee judges the 2022 adjacency to be small, I would not regard a B019 prize as a mistake. But I would not put it ahead of B010, because the evidence for B019 is more indirect.

responses.point: Hassler (chair) ranks B010 first and wants the citation limited to the firm-heterogeneity discovery, not a lifetime-achievement framing for Helpman. He treats Redding as a later quantitative and spatial extension and accepts the precursors' omission as a cost to handle through wording and the scientific background.
responses.response: I agree on all three points. My citation names selection into exporting and the gains from trade, so Helpman is credited for the firm-level and FDI work with Melitz and Yeaple and not for his wider career. On Redding, I answer the chair's question in the negative: I see no specific contribution that makes him co-core, because his quantitative and spatial work builds on the framework. His inclusion would also push the credit to three names without improving the match to the origin of the idea. I would add that handling the precursors through the scientific background is only adequate if the background says plainly what Bernard-Jensen, Eaton-Kortum and Hopenhayn contributed. I note that you are one of the eight B010 supporters and chair the Committee, so I do not read your agreement as independent evidence on merit.

responses.point: Enflo prefers B032 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn after dropping Katz. She argues that the China-shock evidence has been scrutinised for a decade and that debate about magnitudes shows testing, not fragility. She lists B010 as her main alternative.
responses.response: I ranked B032 fifth and proposed the same three names, so we agree on the credit set for the trade-shock core. I accept that continued debate over magnitudes is not by itself a sign of fragility, and that the qualitative finding of slow and costly regional adjustment has survived re-examination. My hesitation comes from my own field's standards on causal identification. Shift-share designs depend on assumptions about exposure and about the exogeneity of the shares, and the long-run welfare picture is unsettled. The entry also still bundles the trade-shock work with the task and skill-demand framework, so the Committee would first have to decide which strand it is rewarding. B010 has the narrower credit question. I think a causal-evidence criterion supports your case, but I weigh it as a strong second-tier alternative and not as ahead of B010.

responses.point: Krusell's opening ranking put B037 first, and his round-1 file moves to B010 because B037's credit is unsettled. He raises field balance after the 2008 trade prize as a consideration and notes Redding and the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum strand as uncredited.
responses.response: I agree with your move on attribution. A prize for B037 would have to defend a three-name boundary against several strong claimants, and the post-2021 inflation questions the baseline model. On field balance, the chair's question asks how it should enter. My view is that significance, attribution and maturity should decide, and field balance should at most be a tie-breaker between candidates the Committee finds close in merit. B010 does not look close to any other candidate on attribution and evidence. I recognise that you raised the point as a consideration, not a conclusion, and I do not claim to have shown it carries no weight.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts that the omitted precursors (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn) can be acknowledged adequately through citation wording and the scientific background, or whether it sees their omission as a defect in the award.

How much of the qualitative selection result and the quantitative gains survive alternative productivity distributions to Pareto. This rests on my recollection and has not been independently verified.
Whether B019 should be preferred if the Committee judges the 2022 prize theme as not close and the accelerator strand (Gertler, Gilchrist) as clearly secondary.
Whether field balance after the 2008 trade prize carries weight with other members that I do not give it.
My assessments rest on recall of the literature and on colleagues' round-1 statements, not on independently verified sources.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Helpman, Melitz, Kiyotaki, Moore, or the credited names on my alternatives B019 and B003 is apparent from my profile. I continue to disclose co-authorship with Torsten Persson, who is credited on B039. B039 is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives, and I do not adjudicate the connection. I also note that I am a Stockholm University colleague of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart, though in a different department. Hassler and Krusell are B010 supporters and Boppart prefers B019, none of them is a candidate, and I disclose this without adjudicating it. My field is political science, not trade or macroeconomics, so my assessment rests on the common criteria and on the colleagues' arguments. My literature judgements are from recall and are unverified.
